intro: Draw what really acts on the block.

widget.instructions: Add each force with Precise controls, choose who exerts it, and set its size and direction. Tick Tilted axes to work along and across the slope. Press Play: a correct diagram keeps the block still.

stem: A {{m}} kg block rests, without moving, on a rough plank tilted at {{theta}}°. Take g = 9.8 m/s².
Draw every force acting on the block, with its size and direction.
answerText: Weight {{W}} N down; normal {{N}} N perpendicular to the plank; friction {{f}} N up the plank.

hints.text: What touches the block? Only the plank. Gravity acts too. The plank can push perpendicular to its surface and along it.
The block is at rest: the net force is zero. Tilt the axes and balance along and across the plank.
Across: N = mg cos θ. Along: friction up the slope = mg sin θ.

normal-equals-weight.text: On a slope the plank pushes back only against the part of the weight pressing into it: N = mg cos θ, not mg.

extra-force-of-motion.text: Nothing pushes the block down the slope except gravity, and gravity is already the weight. The pull down the slope is just the weight's component, not an extra force.

static-friction-always-max.text: Static friction is only as large as needed to stop slipping: here it balances mg sin θ.

friction-direction-opposes-force.text: The block would slide down, so friction acts up the slope.

missing-weight.text: Every body near the Earth has a weight, mg, straight down.

missing-normal.text: The plank pushes on the block perpendicular to its surface.

missing-friction.text: Without friction the block would slide down. The rough plank holds it.

normal-direction.text: The normal force is perpendicular to the plank, not straight up.

double-counted-force.text: The plank gives one normal force and one friction force. Remove the duplicate.

generic.text: Name the agent of each arrow (Earth, plank) and check that the net force is zero.

workedSolution.text: Weight {{W}} N straight down, from the Earth.
Tilted axes. Across the plank: N = mg cos {{theta}}° = {{N}} N.
Along the plank: friction balances mg sin {{theta}}° = {{f}} N, up the slope. Press Play: the block stays still.

generic.front: Forces on a block resting on a rough slope?
generic.back: Weight (down), normal mg cos θ (perpendicular), static friction mg sin θ (up the slope).
